scenario.background: Emily, a manager at a software company, has just hired a new employee named Tom. Tom is hesitant to share his ideas and concerns in meetings, as he fears they won't be taken seriously. Emily wants to convince Tom that his input is valued and will be considered.
scenario.goal: persuade Tom to trust the team and share his ideas

preventive.desire: persuadee wants to avoid embarrassment.

Hi Emily, I just feel like staying silent helps me avoid any potential criticism, and I really don't want to end up embarrassed.

persuader: Absolutely, Tom! Trusting the team and sharing your ideas can introduce fresh perspectives and innovative solutions that might otherwise be overlooked. By contributing, you're actively helping the team achieve its goals and succeed together.
persuadee: I think you're right, Emily. I'll start sharing my ideas at the next meeting and trust the team more.
